$comment: Provenance record for every piece of video material in this directory.
Every clip carries `provenance: real | synthetic`. The report prints it next to every
number derived from the material, and the one-pager prints it next to every claim.
A material with no provenance here is a material whose numbers may not be quoted.

clips.subject: a coloured rectangle crossing a testsrc frame
clips.licence: NOT RECORDED — three fields below are still REPLACE-ME
clips.retrieved: REPLACE-ME — the date it was obtained
clips.attribution: REPLACE-ME — required by the licence if the licence requires it
notes: PROVENANCE CORRECTED. This entry used to say `real`. It does not, and the
correction is not editorial: `testdata/README.md` records a MEASURED run
of this exact clip against a real COCO export, and the model returned ZERO
boxes at all three instants it was pointed at it. A flat coloured
rectangle on a `testsrc` background is not a photograph, and a detector
trained on photographs is right to see nothing in it.
So a row saying `real` beside a clip the model cannot see anything in is
a false label on a measurement, which is the one thing every other rule in
this directory exists to prevent. It is `synthetic` now, and the report
prints `provenance: synthetic` beside every number derived from it.
THE LICENCE IS STILL NOT RECORDED, and that is the blocker, not the
provenance. This clip may be read on the machine that has it and may NOT
be shown to anyone outside it. Three fields above are still `REPLACE-ME`
and until they are filled in a clip with no licence is a clip that cannot
be shown to anyone.
The intended replacement is `testdata/street.mp4`: 60-90 seconds of
daylight footage of a real car or pedestrian crossing a drawn line,
recorded on a phone for this project, with no third-party rights at all.
A detector actually sees daylight footage, which is the whole reason for
the recording.

clips.subject: a bright rectangle travelling left to right
clips.licence: the same licence as this repository
notes: The moving object is a RECTANGLE, not a bird. It has bird-like motion and
bird-like proportions and nothing else.
This clip exists so the pipeline can be exercised end to end on material whose
every property is known. It is NOT evidence that the system detects birds. The
report prints `provenance: synthetic` next to every number derived from it, and
the one-pager says so in words.
The script rebuilds it bit for bit, which is what makes the label checkable rather
than decorative.

clips.subject: a public traffic camera at an intersection, at night, with vehicles crossing
clips.licence: REPLACE-ME — the rights holder is the camera operator, not the uploader, and neither has been asked. This file is NOT committed and is NOT cleared for any use outside this machine.
clips.contains_people: unknown — a night road camera; no pedestrian was observed in the frames examined, and no claim is made that none is present
notes: Downloaded with yt-dlp at operator request. NOT cleared for redistribution, publication
or demonstration to anyone outside this machine, because no permission basis exists:
the camera belongs to a public body, the footage is theirs, and watching it live and
storing clips of it are different acts.
It is used here for ONE reason and it is a good one: it is real footage with real
moving objects, and the committed synthetic material proved nothing about the detector
because a COCO model correctly sees nothing in a coloured rectangle on a testsrc
background. The decoder had a rank bug and a logit bug that this footage exposed
immediately and the synthetic material never could.
provenance: real. Every number the report derives from it is labelled real, and the
false-positive rate is still NOT RUN until a person marks which of the model's 'cars'
are really traffic lights — which, on a night scene with red lights, is very likely
to be several.

car-crossing.mp4.note: The zones file next to the clip is the authority for the geometry. This entry records what a human saw, so a mismatch is detectable. WARNING: the object in this clip is not a vehicle, so a crossing here is a crossing of a RECTANGLE, and it exercises the line-cross machine rather than the detector.

bird-synthetic.mp4.note: The synthetic object travels on a horizontal path at about 0.41 of the frame height, so a horizontal line there is crossed exactly once per pass.

$comment: The intervals in which a crossing is expected, per clip. A run that produces an
event outside every window is a detection the labels did not predict, and the
report should be read with that in mind: an unexpected event is either a
false positive or a mis-drawn line, and only a human can say which.
How long a stored clip may live. The store's sweep is age-based and this is the
age: it never deletes a clip to satisfy a byte target, and it never touches stored
evidence to satisfy the rolling disk ceiling.
